A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EA-KD and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. The original appendix analyses can be matched to Appendix B in v3, supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, object detection, and LLM distillation results, plus ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds ImageNet results, further baseline comparisons, and statistical summaries.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same teacher-entropy base, normalized teacher–student entropy interaction, and weighted distillation loss. EA-TTM applies this existing plug-in procedure; no new algorithmic component is specified.

E1.justification: v3 adds full ImageNet classification with 1.28 million training images, 50,000 validation images, and 1,000 classes (Section 4.1, Table 4), substantially extending classification coverage beyond CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet. Existing detection and five instruction-following datasets remain.

E2.justification: v3 adds TTM and WTTM comparisons on CIFAR-100, DKD as a detection comparator, and DistiLLM's SKLD and SRKLD in LLM evaluation (Appendix A). The new ImageNet comparison also evaluates previously absent comparator configurations KD+LS and DKD+LS, alongside PAD.

E3.justification: The new ImageNet evaluation specifies ResNet34-to-ResNet18 distillation with T′=2. Tiny-ImageNet reporting drops top-5 accuracy, while Figure 5 changes from extreme entropy groups and raw training curves to loss percentages across entropy quartiles. These are bounded protocol extensions and revisions; retained training settings are largely unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 5 replaces the CIFAR-100 top/bottom-10% KLD and convergence analysis with entropy-quartile loss contributions on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet, refining the existing investigation of loss dominance. Temperature/component ablations, β sensitivity, t-SNE analyses, and loss landscapes remain, with the original appendix analyses relocated to Appendix B.

E5.justification: v2 reports averaged benchmark accuracies without their standard deviations. v3 Appendix C adds standard deviations for CIFAR-100 EA-methods over five runs and ImageNet EA-methods over three runs; Table A1 also introduces five-run ± reporting. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting without establishing increased run counts for retained experiments.

E6.justification: v3 adds ImageNet and Appendix A comparison results. Tiny-ImageNet MLD+LS/EA-MLD+LS accuracies change from 56.45/61.93 to 61.36/62.41, reducing the reported gain from 5.48 to 1.05 points; top-5 results disappear. Figure 2a revises entropy-bin accuracies, and Figure 5 replaces training curves. The component ablation changes KD's combined-weight result from 75.27 to 75.46 and FCFD's teacher-only result from 77.37 to 77.50. Table 2 also corrects one gain from +0.09 to +0.10. The PDFs do not explain whether revised experimental scores reflect reruns or corrections.

T1.justification: The entropy and KLD definitions, uniform-student assumption, low/high-entropy derivation, and weighting bounds remain mathematically equivalent. Changed summation indices and the shortened Equation 14 do not introduce or remove substantive mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that jointly using teacher and student entropy enables adaptive sample weighting, improves logit- and feature-based distillation across vision and LLM tasks, and achieves strong performance with negligible overhead. Reworded and reordered contribution bullets preserve these claims.

C2.justification: v3 explains more explicitly how initially high student entropy leaves weighting primarily teacher-guided before adapting during training (Section 4.3). Appendix A interprets the TTM/WTTM comparison as supporting dynamic weighting, and Appendix C adds a qualification about significance testing with mean-only baseline reports.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promise of future code release with a stated repository link. v3 also documents ImageNet's T′ setting and clarifies that the additional LLM comparisons use the same off-policy setting without a pretraining corpus. The latter is newly disclosed information, not evidence of a changed retained LLM procedure.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against PAD, DynamicKD, and TTM/WTTM, distinguishing sample weighting, logit adaptation, entropy regularization, and integration mechanisms. Appendix A.1 develops the TTM/WTTM comparison further. The introduction adds LLM and medical-imaging KD literature, while the earlier MKD and BERT references disappear.

P1.justification: v3 edits the introduction, related work, mechanism discussion, and conclusion, reorders contribution bullets, and organizes supplementary material into comparisons, retained analyses, and statistics. It also updates authorship and corresponding-author text. The main section sequence and much of the narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the displays with ImageNet Table 4, comparison Tables A1–A3, and statistical Tables C4–C5. Figure 5 changes from two wide training panels to four quartile panels; Table 3 loses its top-5 row and average-gain column. Figure 1 is redrawn, and retained appendix figures are relocated and resized.

improvement.justification: ImageNet and the closer baseline comparisons improve validation, while Appendix C makes small gains easier to assess through standard deviations. These extend an already substantial empirical paper. Benefits are tempered by unexplained Tiny-ImageNet score revisions and a new ablation contradiction: Table 9 reports FCFD teacher-only weighting at 77.50 versus 77.44 for combined weighting, despite claiming the combined weighting is superior.
